decisions.rationale: id has null_rate 0.0 and distinct_count 9057 equal to row_count 9057, so it uniquely identifies a row; ident and iata_code also profile as unique and can serve as secondary natural keys, but id is the source's stable surrogate key.
duplicate_row_rate is 0.0 across row_count 9057, so no exact duplicate rows exist in bronze and the dedupe strategy is none.
_airbyte_raw_id, _airbyte_extracted_at, and _airbyte_meta are flagged is_airbyte_metadata and carry no business meaning (_airbyte_meta is constantly '{}'), so all three are dropped.
All id samples are integral digit strings with no nulls, so the landed VARCHAR is cast to INTEGER for stable joins and sort order.
scheduled_service holds exactly two distinct values ('yes', 'no') with null_rate 0.0, so it is renamed to has_scheduled_service and cast to BOOLEAN ('yes' true, 'no' false).

latitude_deg (min -79.777778, max 82.517263) and longitude_deg (min -179.876999, max 179.9757) land as DECIMAL(38,9) but every sample shows at most six decimal places, so they are narrowed to DECIMAL(9,6) and DECIMAL(10,6); elevation_ft samples are all integral so it is cast to INTEGER.

local_code (null_rate 0.636635), keywords (0.679585), and home_link (0.749034) are sparsely populated but carry meaningful values where present, so they are retained nullable with no imputation and no row drops.

purpose: silver_ourairports_airports is a cleaned, one-row-per-airport reference table of 9,057 airports, heliports, and seaplane bases from the OurAirports source, carrying identifiers (id, ident, icao_code, iata_code, gps_code, local_code), classification (type, has_scheduled_service), location (latitude_deg, longitude_deg, elevation_ft, continent, iso_country, iso_region, municipality), and reference links. It feeds downstream dimensional models and geospatial joins that need a conformed airport dimension.
usage: Join on id (the declared grain) or on ident/iata_code, both of which are also unique in this extract. has_scheduled_service is a BOOLEAN derived from the source's yes/no values. Consumers should expect nulls in elevation_ft (~3.7%), municipality (~4.0%), icao_code (~13.7%), gps_code (~5.4%), and especially local_code (~63.7%), keywords (~68.0%), and home_link (~74.9%), and must handle those nulls deliberately rather than assuming full population.
limitations: No deduplication was applied because bronze shows duplicate_row_rate 0.0. Sparse columns (local_code 63.7% null, keywords 68.0% null, home_link 74.9% null) are retained as-is with no imputation. Coordinate precision was narrowed to six decimal places based on sampled values; keywords remains an unparsed comma-separated free-text field. The iata_code uniqueness observed here (9,057 distinct over 9,057 rows) should be re-verified against the full warehouse before being relied on as an alternate key, and the Airbyte capture columns were dropped, so extraction lineage must be traced in bronze.
